name: Cleopatra VII
bio: The last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, famous for her political savvy and alliances with Rome's most powerful men.
fact: She lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.

name: Napoleon Bonaparte
bio: French general who became Emperor of the French and conquered much of Europe.
fact: He was about average height for a Frenchman of his time (around 5 ft 6 in); the 'short' myth came from unit confusion and British cartoons.

name: Isaac Newton
bio: Physicist and mathematician who described gravity and the laws of motion.
fact: Late in life he ran the Royal Mint and personally helped investigate and prosecute counterfeiters.

name: Marie Curie
bio: Pioneering physicist and chemist who researched radioactivity and discovered polonium and radium.
fact: Her laboratory notebooks are still radioactive today and are stored in lead-lined boxes.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
bio: Renaissance painter, inventor and scientist who painted the Mona Lisa.
fact: He wrote his private notebooks in mirror writing, right to left.

name: Albert Einstein
bio: Physicist who developed the theory of relativity.
fact: In 1952 he was offered the presidency of Israel and turned it down.

name: Abraham Lincoln
bio: 16th US president who led the country through the Civil War and ended slavery.
fact: He is an inductee in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame.

name: Benjamin Franklin
bio: Founding father, writer, scientist and inventor who experimented with electricity.
fact: He invented the glass armonica, a musical instrument played with spinning glass bowls, and Mozart wrote music for it.

name: Catherine the Great
bio: Empress of Russia who expanded the empire and championed the arts.
fact: She had herself deliberately inoculated against smallpox in 1768 to encourage her subjects to do the same.

name: Julius Caesar
bio: Roman general and statesman whose rise ended the Roman Republic.
fact: As a young man he was kidnapped by pirates, insisted they ask for a higher ransom, and later hunted them down.

name: Alexander the Great
bio: King of Macedon who built one of the largest empires of the ancient world before age 33.
fact: As a teenager he was personally tutored by the philosopher Aristotle.

name: Queen Victoria
bio: British monarch whose reign of over 63 years gave her name to an era.
fact: She had to propose to Prince Albert herself, because a queen could not be proposed to.

name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
bio: Child prodigy composer who wrote hundreds of works.
fact: At 14 he reportedly wrote out Allegri's guarded Miserere from memory after hearing it once.

name: Ludwig van Beethoven
bio: Composer who bridged the Classical and Romantic eras.
fact: He was almost completely deaf when his Ninth Symphony premiered, and a singer had to turn him around to see the applause.

name: Joan of Arc
bio: Peasant girl who led French armies to victory during the Hundred Years' War.
fact: A retrial in 1456 declared her innocent, about 25 years after she was executed.

name: William Shakespeare
bio: Playwright and poet behind Hamlet, Macbeth and Romeo and Juliet.
fact: In his will he left his wife his 'second-best bed'.

name: Galileo Galilei
bio: Astronomer who used telescopes to support a sun-centered solar system.
fact: He spent his final years under house arrest, and the Vatican formally acknowledged its error in 1992.

name: Harriet Tubman
bio: Escaped slavery and guided many others to freedom on the Underground Railroad.
fact: During the Civil War she served as a Union scout and spy and helped lead a raid that freed more than 700 people.

name: Frida Kahlo
bio: Painter famous for vivid self-portraits.
fact: Her household pets included spider monkeys, a fawn and an eagle.

name: Thomas Edison
bio: Inventor who developed the phonograph and a practical light bulb.
fact: He held 1,093 US patents.

name: Ada Lovelace
bio: Mathematician who worked on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.
fact: She published what is considered the first computer program in 1843, and her father was the poet Lord Byron.

name: Charles Darwin
bio: Naturalist who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection.
fact: As a student at Cambridge he joined a 'Glutton Club' that tried eating hawk and brown owl.

name: Amelia Earhart
bio: Aviation pioneer who disappeared during a flight around the world.
fact: In 1932 she became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.

name: Winston Churchill
bio: British prime minister during most of World War II.
fact: He won the 1953 Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
bio: Leader of India's nonviolent independence movement.
fact: He was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize five times but never won it.

name: Hatshepsut
bio: One of the most successful pharaohs of Egypt's New Kingdom.
fact: She ruled as pharaoh and was often shown wearing the traditional ceremonial false beard.

name: Peter the Great
bio: Tsar who modernised Russia along Western European lines.
fact: He introduced a tax on beards to push Russian nobles to look more European.

name: Henry VIII
bio: English king famous for his six marriages and break with the Catholic Church.
fact: He composed music, and the song 'Pastime with Good Company' is attributed to him.

name: Michelangelo
bio: Sculptor, painter and architect of the Italian Renaissance.
fact: He carved the statue of David from a huge marble block that other sculptors had abandoned.

name: Vincent van Gogh
bio: Post-Impressionist painter known for Starry Night.
fact: He produced roughly 2,000 artworks in about ten years.

name: Rosa Parks
bio: Civil rights activist whose 1955 bus arrest sparked a major protest.
fact: The Montgomery bus boycott that followed her arrest lasted 381 days.

name: Nelson Mandela
bio: Anti-apartheid leader who became South Africa's first Black president.
fact: He spent 27 years in prison before being released in 1990.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
bio: Civil rights leader famous for the 'I Have a Dream' speech.
fact: He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964 at age 35, then the youngest laureate ever.

name: Edgar Allan Poe
bio: Writer of The Raven and macabre short stories.
fact: He once joined the US Army under the false name 'Edgar A. Perry'.

name: Mark Twain
bio: Author of Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn.
fact: He was born in a year Halley's Comet appeared and died the day after it returned in 1910, just as he had predicted.

name: Sacagawea
bio: Shoshone woman who guided the Lewis and Clark expedition.
fact: She travelled with the expedition while carrying her infant son.

name: Grace Hopper
bio: Computer scientist who pioneered programming languages.
fact: She helped develop COBOL and rose to the rank of rear admiral in the US Navy.

name: Tutankhamun
bio: Young pharaoh whose nearly intact tomb was found in 1922.
fact: He became pharaoh at around age nine.

name: The Wright Brothers
bio: Wilbur and Orville, who made the first powered airplane flights in 1903.
fact: They ran a bicycle shop in Dayton, Ohio, before inventing the airplane.

name: Neil Armstrong
bio: Astronaut and first person to walk on the Moon in 1969.
fact: He carried a piece of wood from the Wright brothers' 1903 airplane to the Moon.

name: Wu Zetian
bio: Ruler of China during the Tang dynasty.
fact: She is the only woman to have ruled China as emperor in her own right.

name: Ramesses II
bio: Long-reigning pharaoh nicknamed 'the Great' who built monuments like Abu Simbel.
fact: In 1976 his mummy was issued an official passport so it could fly to Paris for treatment.
